papers.title: An Explainable and Optimized Ensemble Learning Framework Using XGBoost, CatBoost, and LightGBM for Predictive Analytics
papers.abstract: AbstractPredictive analytics on complex tabular datasets is a cornerstone of data-driven decision-making across high-stakes domains including financial risk assessment, healthcare prognostics, and customer intelligence. Although Gradient Boosted Decision Tree (GBDT) architectures—predominantly XGBoost, CatBoost, and LightGBM—exhibit superior empirical predictive power over deep neural networks on tabular structures, three foundational challenges persist: (1) high sensitivity to complex, non-convex hyperparameter spaces; (2) vulnerability to data leakage and validation bias; and (3) a notorious "black-box" opacity that impedes regulatory compliance and clinical adoption. This study proposes an explainable, Bayesian-optimized stacking ensemble learning framework that addresses these challenges systematically. The framework integrates XGBoost, CatBoost, and LightGBM as heterogeneous base-level learners, rigorously tuned via Tree-Structured Parzen Estimator (TPE) Bayesian optimization within an Optuna framework across 50 trials per algorithm under leakage-free nested 5-fold stratified cross-validation. Out-of-fold (OOF) predicted probability vectors are fed into an ElasticNet regularized logistic meta-learner to synthesize orthogonal decision boundaries. Experimental results on an empirical benchmark (N = 30,000) demonstrate that the proposed Stacking Meta-Ensemble outperforms all individual models (ROC-AUC: 0.7891, p < 0.001) while delivering full post-hoc interpretability via TreeSHAP. papers.title: Belief-integrated timed elastic band planning for robust indoor person following under intermittent observations
papers.abstract: Indoor person-following robots routinely lose sight of their target at corners, doorways, and in crowds, and most local planners then stall at the last seen position. We present IO-TEB (Intermittent-Observation Timed Elastic Band), a local planner that maintains a probabilistic estimate of the hidden person’s position and its growing uncertainty, feeds this estimate directly into trajectory optimization, and actively searches likely paths when the person stays hidden. Across 4,320 simulated episodes covering eight indoor scenes, three occlusion durations, and real pedestrian trajectories, IO-TEB completed 87.36% of following tasks, versus 55.14% for the standard timed elastic band planner. It was statistically equivalent to a conventional design that handles the same estimate in a separate finite-state supervisor, indicating that embedding the estimate in the optimizer costs neither accuracy nor computation. Compared with model predictive control (MPC) using trajectory prediction and three recent person-following planners, IO-TEB was not the most accurate, but in our implementation it missed the 100 ms control-cycle deadline least often (3.32% of cycles versus 5.14–44.21%). Ablation shows that replacing the last observation with the predicted estimate as the following reference accounts for most of the gain, whereas the uncertainty-dependent terms added no consistent benefit.

papers.title: Conceptualizing A Closed-Loop Digital Twin for Real-Time Plasma Control in Large-Area Magnetron Sputtering Systems
papers.abstract: Large-area magnetron sputtering underpins the manufacture of architectural low-emissivity glazing, thin-film photovoltaics, flat-panel and flexible displays, and functional coatings, yet the process remains difficult to control at the fidelity that modern device tolerances demand. The governing plasma is a strongly non-linear, spatially distributed, multi-time-scale system in which small excursions in reactive-gas partial pressure, target erosion state, or magnetic-field topology propagate into large deviations in deposition rate, stoichiometry, and thickness uniformity. Conventional single-input single-output feedback loops built around plasma emission monitoring or optical set-points are effective but cannot reason about the unobserved internal state of the discharge, nor anticipate the slow drifts that dominate long production campaigns. This paper conceptualizes a closed-loop digital twin that fuses reduced-order physics-based and data-driven surrogate models of the discharge with heterogeneous in-situ diagnostics through recursive state estimation, and that closes the loop through predictive and learning-based control. We survey the fundamentals of direct-current, radio-frequency, and high-power impulse magnetron sputtering, the hysteresis and instability phenomena that make reactive processes hard to regulate, and the diagnostic instruments—Langmuir probes, optical emission spectroscopy, mass spectrometry, and in-situ metrology—that can supply the twin with real-time observations. Building on the digitaltwin, model-order-reduction, and data-assimilation literatures, we propose a layered architecture spanning the physical asset, a low-latency sensing and data pipeline, coupled twin models, a Kalman-family state estimator, and a control policy realized as model predictive control or reinforcement learning. We define a latency budget across these layers, articulate use cases in uniformity, stoichiometry, arc-suppression, and target-erosion compensation, and set out a validation pathway and research roadmap addressing model fidelity, calibration, uncertainty quantification, verification and validation, and industrial scale-up

papers.title: High-Throughput Polymer Design for the Biological Interface
papers.abstract: Abstract High-throughput experimentation is transforming synthetic polymer design for biological applications, enabling data-driven approaches that map the vast chemical design space accessible to synthetic macromolecules. In this Viewpoint, we survey recent advances in high-throughput methodologies for discovering polymers that interface with biological systems. We first review synthetic strategies, such as well-plate polymerizations, immobilized and solid-phase synthesis, and continuous flow chemistry, that enable parallelized, miniaturized access to large polymer libraries. We then discuss screening methods for structural characterization, target-binding interactions, and functional performance in cellular and biological contexts. We highlight how these readouts capture the disordered, dynamic nature of synthetic polymers relative to structured biomacromolecules. Finally, we examine how machine learning, active learning, self-driving laboratories, and emerging agentic AI tools are being integrated with high-throughput workflows to accelerate inverse design and autonomous experimentation. We underscore the potential of increasingly automated discovery in future years and the need for rigorous, application-appropriate workflow design. Together, these synthesis, characterization, and computational strategies form a synergistic pipeline poised to accelerate the discovery of next-generation polymer therapeutics and biomaterials.

papers.title: Convexity-Preserving Reduced-Complexity Model Predictive Control via Radial Basis Function Networks
papers.abstract: In this study, we investigate Model Predictive Control (MPC) for systems operating under state, control, and output constraints, and propose an enhanced formulation that significantly reduces computational demand. Within the MPC framework, we introduce a novel representation of the control signal based on Radial Basis Function Networks (RBFNs)—well known for their strong function approximation capabilities. Instead of optimizing over a conventional vector of discrete control inputs, the proposed approach encodes the control trajectory using a compact set of RBFN weights. This reformulation substantially decreases the number of optimization variables, thereby reducing the computational burden associated with solving constrained quadratic programs in MPC. The theoretical analysis demonstrates that the transformation from the standard control space to the RBFN weight space preserves convexity and positive definiteness of the original cost function, ensuring stability and uniqueness of the optimal solution. To evaluate the practical benefits of this approach, the MPC–RBFN method is applied to the longitudinal control of an aircraft model. Simulation results confirm that the proposed controller achieves comparable tracking performance to conventional MPC while providing a marked improvement in computational efficiency, highlighting its suitability for real-time and embedded control applications.

papers.title: The laser powder bed fusion of particle-reinforced aluminum alloy matrix composites
papers.abstract: Laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) enables the fabrication of aluminum matrix particulate composites (AMPCs) with opportunities for microstructural refinement and precipitation strengthening. However, reported mechanical responses remain highly non-monotonic with respect to particle content. Strength improvements are often accompanied by limited or inconsistent gains in ductility, fatigue performance, and damage tolerance. This review adopts a constraint-first perspective and organizes the literature along a processing-linked constraint pathway. The performance of LPBF-processed AMPCs is interpreted in terms of a hierarchy of coupled physical constraints that become active at different stages. These include processing stability associated with melting behavior, interfacial mechanical and chemical compatibility under rapid thermal cycling, particle redistribution during melt-pool transport and solidification, and the transition of crack initiation control among competing defect populations. Evidence is synthesized across the full processing chain, from energy coupling at the powder bed to melt-pool dynamics, particle redistribution, and defect evolution. This framework helps explain why particle additions lead to improved mechanical performance in some cases, but not in others where processing-induced constraints become dominant. Based on this synthesis, a transferable design framework is proposed. It emphasizes stable processing conditions, interface states that sustain load transfer, control of particle clustering, and performance evaluation based on defect severity rather than average properties. Overall, this review frames LPBF-processed AMPCs as a constraint-governed system, and provides a basis for interpreting scattered results and improving cross-study comparability.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence in Education: A Review of Learning Analytics, Personalized Tutoring, Generative AI and Academic Integrity
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence now touches most stages of teaching and learning. Learning analytics predicts which students are at risk, knowledge tracing models estimate what each student has mastered, intelligent tutors adapt practice to the learner, and large language models can explain, grade and write. The same tools have created new problems. Generative AI makes it easy to submit text that a student did not write, detection tools are unreliable, and models trained on student data raise questions of privacy and fairness. The problem is that these topics are reviewed in separate literatures: analytics and tutoring surveys rarely discuss academic integrity, and integrity studies rarely discuss the learning models that produce or detect the text. This review brings them into one framework of five layers: learning analytics and prediction, personalization and intelligent tutoring, generative AI in learning, academic integrity, and a cross-cutting layer of privacy, fairness and inclusion. It organizes 42 studies and compares their methods and reported results. Deep knowledge tracing raised the area under the curve from 0.67 to 0.86 over Bayesian knowledge tracing, and intelligent tutoring systems raised test scores by a median of 0.66 standard deviations. A randomized trial found that a carefully designed AI tutor produced learning gains of 0.73 to 1.3 standard deviations over in-class active learning, but a field experiment found that unrestricted GPT-4 access raised practice grades by 48% and then lowered exam grades by 17%. Detection of AI-generated text is weak: tested tools were neither accurate nor reliable, and detectors flagged 61% of essays by non-native English writers as machine-written. Few studies connect personalization with integrity or measure bias across student groups. Future work should design AI tutors with learning safeguards, assess integrity through process rather than detection alone, and evaluate both under privacy protection and across diverse learners.

papers.title: An Intelligent Cyber–Physical Framework for Electric Bus Batteries: Combining DQN Smart Charging with LSTM Digital Twins
papers.abstract: The operational reliability of electric buses depends heavily on the thermal stability and longevity of their battery packs. In urban public transit, highly dynamic driving cycles characterized by severe current surges during regenerative braking and prolonged constantcurrent charging phases induce massive localized thermal stress. Traditional battery management systems often fail to dynamically balance energy recovery with the physical constraints of cell matrices, leading to accelerated degradation and potential safety hazards. This paper proposes an integrated cyber–physical framework that merges intelligent control with advanced prognostic monitoring and predictive thermal management. The core of the control layer is a deep Q-network (DQN) agent designed for real-time smart charging and dynamic regenerative braking current limitation (smart derating). This control loop is tightly integrated with a long short-term memory (LSTM) network-based digital twin (DT) operating at the edge level to mirror complex electro-thermal dynamics and track the battery state of health (SOH). To ensure transparency and proactive thermal control, a nonlinear model predictive control (NMPC) strategy is implemented, utilizing SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) to map core heat generation and dynamically adjust for internal thermal lag. The predictive NMPC-xAI loop maintained cell temperatures within a tight, optimal envelope, preventing delayed under-cooling and reducing peak temperature fluctuations

papers.title: A conformal virtual metrology framework for predictive uncertainty quantification: a full factorial experimental study of micro crown gear quality
papers.abstract: Abstract Virtual metrology uses process data to estimate product quality before physical measurement results become available. However, most models return only a point prediction, which does not show whether an individual prediction is reliable enough for quality decisions. This paper develops a conformal prediction framework for virtual metrology of micro crown gear quality from acoustic emission signals. The framework combines regression pipelines selected for each quality characteristic with Split conformal prediction (Split CP), cross validation plus (CV+), and cross fitted conformalized quantile regression (CF-CQR). The framework is model agnostic and does not require a parametric form for the distribution of the data. Under exchangeability, conformal prediction provides finite sample marginal coverage guarantees for prediction intervals. Split CP, CV+ and CF-CQR are evaluated over repeated data partitions of the full-factorial experimental dataset using empirical coverage, interval width, and the Winkler score. The results show that acoustic emission signals support the prediction of the studied geometric characteristics, although predictive difficulty varies across targets. The conformal methods provide coverage close to the nominal level, while cross validation plus and cross fitted conformalized quantile regression generally produce more informative intervals than Split conformal prediction. The predicted intervals are used to formulate an interpretable quality assessment logic by distinguishing clear conformity, clear nonconformity, and ambiguous cases that require physical measurement or expert assessment. The proposed framework moves virtual metrology from isolated point predictions towards quality predictions that communicate uncertainty explicitly.

papers.title: The Effectiveness of Interactive Digital Learning Media in Increasing High School Students' Learning Motivation
papers.abstract: Digital transformation encourages the use of increasingly interactive learning media, but its effectiveness on student learning motivation is still determined by the pedagogical design and context of use. This study aims to analyze the effectiveness of interactive digital learning media in improving learning motivation of high school students. The study used a quantitative approach with a quasi-experimental pretest-posttest control group design. A total of 120 10th grade students from four high schools in Ambon City, Maluku Province, participated in the study. Schools were selected purposively based on the readiness of digital learning facilities, while classes were selected through cluster sampling; 60 students were in the experimental group and 60 students in the control group. The experimental group participated in Indonesian language learning on the topic of explanatory text using digital media that integrated videos, visual materials, digital quizzes, interactive exercises, and direct feedback for six meetings, while the control group participated in regular learning with the same materials and time allocation. Learning motivation was measured using a five-point Likert scale questionnaire and data were analyzed using Analysis of Covariance (ANCOVA). The motivation score of the experimental group increased from 3.18 to 4.08, while the control group increased from 3.21 to 3.39. After controlling for baseline scores, there was a significant difference between the two groups, F (1,117) = 79.62, p < 0.001, ηp² = 0.405. The largest difference was found in the engagement and interest dimensions. The findings indicate that, in this study sample, interactive digital learning media was associated with higher motivational increases when technology was used to support active learning activities and provide feedback.

papers.title: The GATE Framework: A Generative AI-Enhanced Active Learning Environment for Tourism Communication Competency Development
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is being adopted in tourism and hospitality education more quickly than the pedagogical guidance needed to use it well. This study developed the GATE Framework, a GenAI-enhanced active learning environment intended to develop tourism communication competency, and examined its appropriateness through expert review. The work comprised two stages within the first research phase. An evidence-informed synthesis established three connected layers: Inputs, Core Process Components, and Outcomes. At the center of the Process Layer is an iterative Explore-Generate-Apply-Reflect cycle, supported by human-AI interaction, authentic tourism tasks, peer and instructor participation, reflection, and adaptive feedback. In the second stage, nine experts in tourism and hospitality, curriculum and instruction, educational technology, AI in education, and active learning then evaluated the framework using an 18-item, five-point scale and four open-ended questions. The overall rating was very high (x̄ = 4.54, S.D. = 0.58), and the five domain means ranged from 4.52 to 4.56. The experts gave their strongest ratings to the framework's theoretical alignment, relevance to tourism communication learning, and suitability for further development. Ratings remained favorable but were lower for the definition of individual roles and the practical sequence of the learning process. In response, the framework was revised to clarify scaffolding and human oversight, strengthen privacy and transparency provisions, and give greater weight to tourism content rooted in local culture. The resulting framework provides the conceptual basis for GATE-SLE, where GenAI assists disciplinary learning without displacing human judgment.

papers.title: A Statistical Reliability Framework for Markov Epidemic Networks
papers.abstract: Disease progression can be statistically represented as a network of patient states connected by transition probabilities, providing a natural basis for quantifying progression toward favorable and unfavorable outcomes. This study develops a statistical reliability framework for disease progression networks based on discrete-time Markov transitions, integrating maximum-likelihood estimation, first-passage reliability, bootstrap uncertainty quantification, and probability-simplex-constrained sensitivity analysis. The framework converts patient-level longitudinal trajectories into an estimated transition structure and subsequently quantifies the probability of reaching a favorable target state before an absorbing unfavorable outcome. A row-preserving perturbation strategy is used to assess the influence of individual transitions while maintaining the probability constraints, and a dimensionless elasticity measure is introduced to rank transitions according to their contribution to network reliability. Monte Carlo experiments demonstrate stable statistical performance of the proposed estimator: for the specified baseline network, the true reliability is approximately 0.7483, while the RMSE decreases from 0.0465 for n=100 to 0.0098 for n=2000, indicating substantial improvement in estimation accuracy as the sample size increases. The sensitivity analysis further identifies the most influential transitions, with progression from localized disease to treatment and treatment to remission showing the strongest positive effects on reliability, whereas transitions toward death exhibit negative effects. The framework is also applied to a real longitudinal breast cancer dataset comprising 169 patient records. The empirical analysis identifies 16 recurrence events and four deaths and characterizes the observed treatment, surgery, recurrence, and survival-time patterns. Importantly, because the available clinical variables do not unambiguously identify all states of the theoretical seven-state model, the real-data analysis is restricted to directly observable patient events rather than imposing unsupported clinical state assignments. Overall, the results demonstrate that the proposed framework provides a statistically interpretable pipeline linking patient-level transition data, network reliability, uncertainty quantification, and transition importance, with potential applications to reliability-based analysis of multistate disease progression and other longitudinal health processes.

papers.title: A Bibliometric and Network Analysis of Statistical Distributions in Machine Learning
papers.abstract: Statistical distributions constitute a fundamental component of machine learning by providing the probabilistic framework required for modelling uncertainty, variability, and data-generating processes. They underpin a wide range of methodologies, including Bayesian inference, probabilistic graphical models, generative learning and uncertainty-aware artificial intelligence. Despite their widespread application, the evolution and intellectual structure of research on statistical distributions in machine learning have not been systematically examined. This study presents a bibliometric and network analysis of 840 Scopus-indexed publications published between 1997 and 2025. Bibliographic data were analysed using Biblioshiny and VOS viewer to evaluate publication trends, influential sources, author productivity, collaboration patterns and thematic developments. Descriptive indicators were complemented by co-authorship, co-citation, keyword co-occurrence and thematic analyses to explore the social and intellectual structure of the field. The findings reveal sustained growth in research output, increasing international collaboration and the dominance of a core set of journals and authors. Network analyses identify probabilistic modelling, Bayesian learning, uncertainty quantification and generative approaches as the principal intellectual foundations of the field. The results further indicate a gradual shift from classical statistical learning frameworks toward uncertainty-aware and explainable machine learning paradigms. By mapping the evolution, knowledge structure and emerging directions of this research domain, the study provides a comprehensive reference for future investigations at the intersection of statistical distribution theory and machine learning.

papers.title: Prognostic maintenance and smart monitoring of solar panel using IoT devices and hybrid machine learning models
papers.abstract: The profusion, flexibility, and recurrently declining installation costs of solar photovoltaic (PV) technology have made it a protuberant renewable energy source. However, environmental unpredictability, component deterioration, power-electronic failures, and aging effects continue to have a major impact on the long-term performance and reliability of PV systems. There are some drawbacks to the conventional maintenance techniques employed in PV installations, such as routine manual inspections and corrective actions. In order to improve the performance and operational efficiency of solar PV systems, this work presents a prognostic maintenance framework driven by machine learning techniques and enabled by IoT device. A low cost hardware prototype of real time solar data acquisition and monitoring system is developed using LoRa module which collects data from the solar station and in the transmitter station the data is pushed to cloud and displayed in dashboard. Different machine learning models linear regression, decision tree, random forest and XGBoost has been implemented for predictive maintenance of solar panels. A hybrid machine learning model based on Bayesian optimization of XGBoost is proposed and from the comparative assessment of the machine learning models it is validated that the proposed hybrid model showed superior performance in terms of highest accuracy and lowest computation time.

papers.title: Potential of the Discovery Learning Model with a Cognitive Conflict Approach on Students’ Problem-Solving Skills: A Review
papers.abstract: Problem-solving skills are one of the key 21st-century competencies that can be developed through active learning. Although various studies have demonstrated the positive impact of the discovery learning model on problem-solving skills, research that integrates current trends with a synthesis of findings regarding the role of learning approaches- particularly the cognitive conflict approach-remains limited. This study aims to analyze trends in research on the discovery learning model as it relates to students’ problem-solving skills and to examine trends in the integration of learning approaches that support its implementation. The method used is a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) based on the PRISMA framework combined with bibliometric analysis. Bibliometric data were obtained from the Scopus database and analyzed using VOSviewer and Biblioshiny. Meanwhile, thematic analysis was conducted on 22 selected articles from Google Scholar and Scopus. Bibliometric findings suggest that research on discovery learning and problem-solving skills remains an active area of study, particularly in science and chemistry education. Recent research has explored the use of discovery learning alongside various approaches and strategies to promote active learning. Thematic synthesis further shows that discovery learning has generally been found to be effective in improving students' problem-solving skills. It can also be improved by using the right media, learning strategies, and teaching methods. The cognitive conflict method of learning, among others, has been highlighted in the literature as a learning approach that fits here, since it enables the restructuring of concepts.

papers.abstract: The school-based oral health promoting program was developed to build oral health literacy among upper primary school students with health teachers delivering the program alongside a digital platform through active learning. This activity format has a single nationwide standard, with health teachers serving as the main party responsible for its implementation in each school. This qualitative study aimed to analyze the inequality in the adaptation burden faced by health teachers in carrying out this activity, under varying levels of resource readiness across different school contexts covering readiness, obstacles, support networks, and the approaches health teachers propose for the program's sustainability. Data were collected using purposive sampling with maximum variation, drawn from 6 primary schools across 4 regions with differing levels of cooperation and resource readiness. The main informants were 14 health teachers, supplemented by data from 7 school administrators to provide context on the management environment. In-depth interviews adapted from the CIPP Model framework were used, with data analyzed through thematic analysis and credibility verified through triangulation until data saturation was reached. The findings showed that the health teachers' adaptation burden was concentrated among health teachers in small schools and rural areas with more limited resources. This can be summarized into 5 main themes: 1) Factors that help reduce the adaptation burden; 2) Compensatory adaptation burdens falling on teachers in resource-scarce schools; 3) Reliance on external dental personnel networks, whose continuity varied unevenly across areas; 4) Teachers' perception of positive outcomes on students' oral health behavior even in resource-limited schools; and 5) Approaches proposed by teachers to reduce the inequality of the adaptation burden The findings indicate that sustainable policy design should be flexible and allocate support according to each area's level of need, rather than leaving health teachers to face the adaptation burden alone.

papers.title: Hybrid Biofabrication of a Hierarchically Organized Periosteum-Inspired In Vitro Platform.
papers.abstract: The periosteum is a hierarchically organized, vascularized membrane essential for skeletal maintenance and regeneration, yet in vitro models that reproduce its compartmentalized and multicellular architecture remain limited. In this study, we present a hierarchically organized, periosteum-inspired in vitro platform fabricated by integrating melt electrowriting (MEW) with extrusion-based 3D bioprinting. The platform integrates a human osteoblast-laden plasma-containing alginate/methylcellulose hydrogel compartment, a configurable MEW-PCL microfibrous interface, and an endothelial cell-fibroblast-laden fibrin/gelatin hydrogel compartment. MEW scaffold architectures and compartment-specific bioink-cell configurations were screened based on their ability to support osteogenic maturation-associated readouts and CD31+ endothelial cell organization. The resulting tri-layer construct maintained high cytocompatibility and structural integrity during culture for up to 49 days. The osteogenic compartment supported osteogenic differentiation-associated readouts and mineralized matrix deposition, while the endothelial cell-containing compartment supported interconnected CD31+ endothelial cell organization accompanied by endothelial cell-associated gene expression. Overall, this hybrid MEW-3D bioprinted platform provides an engineerable in vitro model for periosteum-inspired tissue modeling, biomaterial screening, and investigation of osteogenic and endothelial cell-associated processes under controlled conditions.

papers.title: Teriparatide Topical Delivery Supports Osseointegration in Ovariectomized Rats Receiving Cafeteria Diet and Bisphosphonate: An In Vivo Experimental Study.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Postmenopausal osteoporosis associated with cafeteria diet and bisphosphonate therapy may impair peri-implant bone repair. Therefore, strategies to enhance osseointegration are needed. AIM: This study investigated whether teriparatide-coated implant surfaces enhance osseointegration in a rodent model of estrogen deficiency (OVX) and cafeteria diet (CD) treated with risedronate (RIS). MATERIAL AND METHODS: In the in vitro phase, titanium discs coated with 10 or 40 ng of teriparatide were evaluated by in vitro bioassays, and drug adsorption was confirmed by UV-Vis spectroscopy. As both loading amounts produced similar biological responses, 10 ng was selected for the in vivo phase. In the in vivo phase, 48 rats were randomly assigned to SHAM (sham-operated control), OVX/CD (ovariectomized with cafeteria diet), or OVX/CD/RIS (ovariectomized with cafeteria diet and risedronate) groups. Titanium implants either coated with teriparatide using a layer-by-layer topical drug delivery system or left non-coated were placed bilaterally in the maxilla. Rats were euthanized after 28 days. Osseointegration was evaluated by removal torque testing, micro computed tomography, fluorescence microscopy, and RT-qPCR analysis. RESULTS: In the cell culture experiment, both teriparatide amounts successfully promoted mineralized nodule formation in vitro and UV-Vis spectroscopy confirmed drug adsorption. In vivo, teriparatide significantly increased removal torque across all groups, with the greatest increase in OVX/CD/RIS. Teriparatide also increased peri-implant bone volume in OVX/CD and OVX/CD/RIS, confirmed by micro computed tomography and fluorescence microscopy. RT-qPCR also confirmed upregulation of osteogenic and angiogenic markers. CONCLUSION: Topical teriparatide delivery improves peri-implant bone repair under estrogen deficiency, cafeteria diet, and bisphosphonate therapy.
